label: World Championships — Individual
why: Official FIE format for Senior World Championships individual events (Mixed Formula A, FIE Organisation Rules o.83-88): a preliminary phase (pools, then a preliminary tableau) narrows the field to 64, who then fence a main tableau straight through to the final. Identical shape to Grand Prix and World Cup below — FIE's own rule text names all three together as one formula.
note: Uses the fixed 70% pool-advancement shape (same as Grand Prix). o.86.1 permits Worlds/World Cup a 70-80% range; percentage-range advancement isn't built yet (see docs/format-system-comparison.md §8).

label: World Cup — Individual
why: Official FIE format for Senior World Cup individual events (Mixed Formula A, o.83-88) — the exact same shape as World Championships and Grand Prix. Pick this one for a World Cup specifically; it exists mainly for clarity in the picker, since the underlying pipeline doesn't differ from the other two.
note: Uses the fixed 70% pool-advancement shape (same as Grand Prix). o.86.1 permits Worlds/World Cup a 70-80% range; percentage-range advancement isn't built yet (see docs/format-system-comparison.md §8).

label: Grand Prix — Individual
why: Official FIE format for Grand Prix individual events (Mixed Formula A, o.83-88). This is the one tier where the 70% pool-advancement used here is exactly what the rule mandates, not just a legal choice within a range — o.86.1 pins Grand Prix to 30% eliminated (70% advance) specifically, unlike Worlds/World Cup which permit 70-80%.

label: World Championships — Junior Individual
why: Official FIE format for Junior World Championships individual events (Mixed Formula B, o.89-94): one pool round, then a single direct-elimination tableau straight through to the final — no separate preliminary/main split like Formula A above, and no bronze bout (o.94: semifinal losers share 3rd).

label: World Championships — Cadet Individual
why: Official FIE format for Cadet World Championships individual events — FIE's rule (o.89) groups Junior and Cadet Worlds under the same Mixed Formula B; this entry and 'World Championships — Junior Individual' above use the identical shape.

label: World Cup — Junior Individual
why: Official FIE format for Junior World Cup individual events — same Mixed Formula B as the Worlds entries above (o.89 groups Cadet/Junior World Cup in with Junior/Cadet Worlds and Zonal Championships as one formula).

label: World Cup — Cadet Individual
why: Official FIE format for Cadet World Cup individual events — same Mixed Formula B as every other entry in this group (o.89-94).

label: Zonal Championships — Individual
why: Official FIE format for Zonal Championships individual events — same Mixed Formula B shape as Junior/Cadet Worlds and World Cup (o.89-94). FIE's rule text doesn't split Zonal Championships by age category the way Worlds/World Cup are split, so there's one entry here rather than a Junior/Cadet pair.

label: Veterans — Individual
why: Approximates FIE Veterans individual events (o.114-118): a pool round where 100% advance (o.118.7: 'no fencer is eliminated after the pools'), then a straight DE tableau with everyone. Use this instead of the generic 'Pools then DE' entry below when you specifically want the no-elimination Veterans behavior as the default.
note: 100% pool advancement approximates o.118.7's 'no fencer is eliminated after the pools.' Doesn't model o.118's category-merge-below-6 or poule-unique-below-10 edge cases.

label: Pools then DE (choose advancement %)
why: General-purpose format for club/regional events where the pool-advancement percentage isn't fixed by a specific rule — you choose the cut (e.g. 70%, 80%) when applying it. Use the FIE-tier entries above instead if you need a specific official percentage guaranteed rather than a free choice.

label: Two Pool Rounds (combined seeding) then DE
why: Two full pool rounds; the final tableau is seeded by each fencer's COMBINED statistics ADDED TOGETHER across both pool rounds (sometimes called the 'Brazilian' format). Differs from 'round-2 seeding' below, which only uses the second round's own ranking and discards the first round's stats once it's decided who advances.

label: Two Pool Rounds (round-2 seeding) then DE
why: Two full pool rounds; the final tableau is seeded ONLY by the second pool round's own ranking — the first round only decides who advances to round 2, its stats don't carry forward into seeding at all. Differs from 'combined seeding' above, which adds both rounds' statistics together.

label: Pool Round then Level Pools
why: One pool round, then everyone is regrouped into a second round of pools formed from blocks of similarly-ranked fencers (e.g. ranks 1-6 together, 7-12 together) instead of the usual spread-out seeding. That second round of pools IS the final ranking — there is no DE tableau at all in this format.

label: Pools then DE with repechage (T32→T8)
why: Pools, then a DE tableau where losers get a second chance: fencers eliminated between the round of 32 and the round of 8 fence a repechage bracket, and its winners REJOIN the main survivors to fight for the final places together. Unlike the Division/Elite-Division formats, repechage always merges back into one shared final — it never produces two separate winners. Smaller repechage cascade than the T64→T4 entry below.

label: Pools then DE with repechage (T64→T4, classic épée)
why: Same repechage mechanism as the T32→T8 entry above, but starting from a much larger T64 tableau and only rejoining at the final four — losers from T64, T32, T16, and T8 all feed the repechage cascade. This is the classic historical FIE épée repechage shape; use the T32→T8 entry instead for a smaller, shorter repechage.

label: Pools then DE, all places fenced from T16
why: Pools, then a DE tableau where every place from 9th downward is decided by an actual bout instead of being shared — round-of-16 losers fence their own mini-bracket for 9th-16th, round-of-8 losers for 5th-8th, and so on. Use this when every competitor needs a fully individual final rank, not just the top few places.

label: Two Pool Rounds then DE with repechage (T32→T8)
why: Combines two ideas above: two pool rounds (combined seeding) feeding a T32→T8 repechage tableau instead of a plain DE. Use this instead of the single-pool-round repechage entry when you want a second pool round to refine seeding before the tableau.

label: Two Pool Rounds then DE, all places fenced from T16
why: Combines two ideas above: two pool rounds (combined seeding) feeding an all-places-fenced tableau instead of a plain DE. Use this instead of the single-pool-round all-places-fenced entry when you want a second pool round to refine seeding first.

label: Pools (top 8 advance) then DE, bronze bout
why: Pools, then only the top 8 fencers by pool ranking advance — a fixed HEADCOUNT, not a percentage, so the tableau size never changes regardless of how many entered. Use 'Pools then DE (choose advancement %)' above instead if you want the cut to scale with field size.

label: Pools (top 16 advance) then DE, bronze bout
why: Same as 'top 8 advance' above but the cut is a fixed 16 fencers instead of 8.

label: Straight Direct Elimination, bronze bout
why: No pool round at all — straight into a direct-elimination tableau seeded from initial ranking, with a bronze-medal bout between the two semifinal losers. Use 'no bronze bout' below if you'd rather the two semifinal losers simply share 3rd place.

label: Straight Direct Elimination, no bronze bout
why: Same as 'bronze bout' above — no pool round, straight DE from initial ranking — except the two semifinal losers share 3rd place instead of fencing a decider.

label: Division 1 (top 16) / Division 2 — independent tableaux
why: Splits the field by INITIAL SEED, before anyone fences, into two fully independent competitions — Division 1 (seeds 1-16) and Division 2 (the rest) — each with its own complete DE tableau and its own separate winner. They never interact; Division 1 is simply listed ahead of Division 2 in the results. Differs from 'Pool Round then Elite Division / Division 1' below, which splits by POOL RESULT and runs a pool round first instead of skipping straight to DE.
note: Two fully independent competitions run in parallel from one rank split. Division 1 (ranks 1-16) is reported ahead of Division 2 in the results.

label: Pool Round then Elite Division / Division 1 — independent tableaux
why: Runs one pool round first (nobody is eliminated by it — it exists purely to rank the field), then splits into two independent tableaux by that POOL RESULT: Elite Division (top 16 by pool ranking) and Division 1 (the rest). Differs from 'Division 1 / Division 2' above, which splits by initial seed and has no pool round at all.
note: One pool round (no elimination, used only to rank the field), then split by pool result into two fully independent tableaux — top 16 (Elite Division) and the rest (Division 1). Elite Division is reported ahead of Division 1 in the results.
